_meta.drift_contract: `--check` compares the code-derived topology (surfaces, writers, readers, violations, overlaps, retired surfaces, coverage) and, only when the runtime probe is available, the service unit/port set. Per-service pid and invocation_id are observations and are never compared.

canonical_ownership.staged_note: lilac-srv (plan 8261669) is the typed idempotent surface the canonical implementation is moving to. It is staged-inert: no live caller is repointed at it. Declared here so the transition is recorded rather than appearing as an undeclared writer.
canonical_ownership.statement: Lilac owns ticket, receipt, execution-claim and fan-out behavior. The one canonical implementation lives in python/conduit/lilac.py; the typed surface it is moving to is typescript/lilac-srv (staged-inert, plan 8261669). Every other module that mutates those surfaces is either a declared compatibility seam, a legacy writer pending redirect, or a violation recorded below.

overlaps.reason: TypeScript writers still target the legacy vision.receipts store; the one canonical stream is resolution.receipt, written by the Lilac adapter. Redirect is carried by plan 8261669 (L3).
TypeScript writers still target legacy vision/wind ticket stores; canonical ticket persistence is the Lilac adapter. Redirect is carried by plan 8261669 (L3).

Both python/conduit/lilac.py (live) and the staged lilac-srv repository write resolution.ticket_transition under the same natural key (ticket_id, from, to, input_receipt, policy), so a replay classifies identically on either path. Intentional during the cutover; the surface becomes the writer when 8261669's activation gate is opened.

Both writers record the receipt-to-ticket ledger under (input_receipt_id, kind, policy_version); the ledger is the single fan-out record either way, so having two implementations of one ledger is a cutover channel, not a second authority.
